messages:
sam.k: Quick follow-up from the RFC review — proposing we refactor the enrichment pipeline to an explicit dependency graph instead of the current ad-hoc chained handlers. Reason: clearer contracts, easier incremental rollout, and better cost attribution.
marta: can you sketch the contract you have in mind? main pain for us has been nondeterministic ordering and hidden KV cache coupling.
sam.k: yep. rough idea: each enrichment is a node with (reads: keys it needs, writes: keys it produces, idempotent: bool). runtime constructs DAG per request using available nodes, then schedules passes. this lets us: 1) parallelize independent nodes 2) persist intermediate keys for caching 3) compute per-node cost/latency metrics.
raj: sounds promising. two quick concerns: 1) how do we handle side-effecting enrichments (calls that mutate external systems)? 2) what about ordering-sensitive transformations (e.g., normalization then sentiment)?
olivia: for side-effects we should mark nodes as "side_effect=true" and force sequential execution + retry semantics. and we must expose that flag to customers (so they can opt-in or we can run them in a separate sandboxed phase).
sam.k: exactly. ordering-sensitive nodes get an explicit dependency edge. Normalization -> sentiment would be enforced by DAG. For partially ordered sets we allow logical groups with a stable scheduler.
marta: example envelope shape? sharing what we've been using causes confusion since some services expect root fields and others expect enrichments in .enrichments.
sam.k: proposal for canonical envelope (small):

```json
{
  "request_id": "<uuid>",
  "trace_id": "<hex>",
  "payload": { /* original request */ },
  "enrichments": {
    "norm.v1": {"status":"ready","value": {...}},
    "ner.v2":  {"status":"pending"}
  },
  "billing": {"node_costs":[], "total_tokens":""}
}
```

Key points: enrichments keyed by node name+version, status enum (pending/ready/failed), and a billing.node_costs array we can use to attribute token/time to nodes.
raj: 👍 I like node-versioning for rollout. How do we plan the migration? big bang will break many consumers.
sam.k: migration plan: 1) Add graph mode behind feature flag (no-op single-pass compatibility DAG that mimics current chaining). 2) Add node-level telemetry and billing fields (opt-in). 3) Enable multi-pass scheduling for internal services first (dev/prod canary). 4) Gradually require consumers to read canonical envelope keys; provide adapters for older shapes.
olivia: who will own adapters? ingestion team or each downstream? I vote for central adaptor library + thin per-service shims.
marta: agree. central lib reduces duplication. also need linting/validation hooks so incorrect shapes fail CI.
ingest-bot: deploy-notify: schema-validator v2.1 promoted to staging at 2026-03-19T11:02Z
raj: performance question — multi-pass could increase latency if we wait for sequential nodes. How do we preserve SLOs?
sam.k: scheduler heuristics: prefer merge-then-execute for latency-critical flows (combine cheap transforms in same pass). also allow per-route policy: "latency_slo": "200ms" will force eager execution and possibly bypass some heavy offline enrichments.
olivia: and for cost we can run heavy enrichments in background with eventual consistency and mark status=stale until ready. gives UX tradeoffs.
marta: testing matrix: unit for node contracts, integration for DAG producer, perf tests on a representative sample workload, and regression alerts for per-node token cost.
raj: +1. Also add a rollout canary that verifies billing attribution before we flip for all tenants.
sam.k: next steps: I'll open a short RFC PR with the envelope schema and scheduler API today. request volunteers for a 1-hr design sync Wed. action items: @marta owner for validation library, @raj owner for perf harness, @olivia owner for adapter library.
marta: I can pick up validation lib. will post design notes by EOD.
olivia: I'll prototype adapter shim and share a minimal npm pkg.
raj: will scaffold perf tests and run a baseline by Friday.
sam.k: thanks — will post the PR link here once ready. :thumbsup:
